summary: Iter35 – Razorpay ISOLATED PSP plugin verification. Added test_iter35_razorpay.py with 26 tests (25 passed, 1 real functional failure: cumulative refund cap not enforced). Re-ran iter32/33/34 regression: iter32=24/24 PASS, iter33/34 failures are pre-existing environment/seed regressions from the DB reset (missing acme sandbox UPI acceptance account, missing captest tenant) — NOT caused by the razorpay plugin. Confirmed (1) no razorpay-specific code leaked into engine/registry/wizard/webhook core, and (2) LIVE httpx path exercised via mocks only – no real network calls.

critical.issue: Cumulative refund cap NOT enforced for razorpay (and likely any plugin whose refund adapter returns status='refunded'). create_refund() aggregates prior refunds with 'Refund.status == "succeeded"' filter, but RazorpayProvider.refund() sets ProviderResult.status='refunded' -> Refund row is persisted with status='refunded', so 'already' is always 0. Test: partial 5000 then over-refund 20000 on a 20000 razorpay card payment succeeded (should be 400). File/line: app/services/payment_engine.py:259-263.

regression_iter32_33_34.iter33: 16/18 PASS, 2 FAIL — both are TestTenantIsolation ops-cannot-read (captest_id fixture falls back to platform tenant since CapTest tenant was removed during DB reset; NOT razorpay-related).
regression_iter32_33_34.iter34: 17/25 collected — 4 ERRORS (TestAcceptanceMapping: 'acme should have a sandbox UPI acceptance account seeded' — no seed rows exist in payment_acceptance_accounts for acme after reset; NOT razorpay-related) + 1 FAIL (TestPermissionIsolation same captest fallback issue) + 20 PASS.
regression_iter32_33_34.conclusion: All regression FAILs/ERRORs are traceable to the acknowledged tenant/seed reset (captest tenant gone, no acme sandbox UPI acceptance account seeded). None are caused by registering RazorpayProvider.

isolation_confirmations.no_razorpay_code_in_core: Verified by TestNoCoreLeakage.test_no_razorpay_in_core_engine (grep of payment_engine.py, registry.py, config.py) — no 'provider_key == "razorpay"' or similar branches. Registry.py contains ONLY register(RazorpayProvider()).
isolation_confirmations.live_path_never_hit_real_network: TestLivePathMocked patches httpx.request; confirmed create_payment LIVE branch calls POST https://api.razorpay.com/v1/orders with Basic auth (key_id, key_secret) and returns pending — no fallback to sandbox on failure. test_live_missing_creds_raises_ProviderError confirms hard fail (never silent-sandbox).

action_items: FIX (payment_engine.create_refund): normalize the cumulative-refunded aggregation to also count Refund.status in ('succeeded','refunded','partially_refunded'), OR normalize RazorpayProvider.refund() to return ProviderResult.status='succeeded'. As-is, razorpay refunds bypass the cumulative cap.
SEED (env, pre-existing): re-seed acme.payment_acceptance_accounts (sandbox UPI) or update iter34's TestAcceptanceMapping fixture to create the account inline. This unblocks 4 ERRORs.

TESTS (env, pre-existing): iter33/iter34 tenant-isolation tests reference the now-removed 'captest' tenant and silently fall back to 'platform' (a tenant the ops user belongs to), turning 403 checks into 200. Update fixtures to create a second non-platform tenant or skip when unavailable.
critical_code_review_comments: Refund status normalization inconsistency across plugins: RazorpayProvider.refund returns status='refunded' in sandbox and _status.to_cloudpay_status('processed')='refunded' in live; MockProvider returns 'succeeded'. The core aggregation in create_refund only counts 'succeeded' -> over-refund is possible for razorpay. Either the plugin contract should mandate a single terminal status (e.g. 'succeeded') OR the aggregation must be status-agnostic.

razorpay_provider.verify_callback pops '_webhook_secret' from body before HMAC check (test hook). Good – but if a genuine razorpay live webhook ever contained a '_webhook_secret' key it would be silently stripped. Consider gating this to non-live only, or renaming the hook to a more collision-safe key.

razorpay_provider.RazorpayStatusMapper maps 'processed' -> 'refunded'. That matches razorpay's refund lifecycle, but the same mapper is used for payment.status too; a payment reaching status 'processed' would be treated as 'refunded'. Consider separate maps for payment vs refund status.
razorpay_provider._RazorpayApiClient.request has no retry/backoff; single-shot 30s timeout. Fine for phase-2 but future consideration.
